provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: BECE comprehension marathon
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state two strategies for managing time during BECE comprehension.
The students should be able to identify main ideas in a passage.
The students should be able to answer questions based on a comprehension passage.
Introduction:
We have learned how to read and understand passages in our previous lessons. Today we will focus on how to handle comprehension passages during the BECE examination.
Content:
Time management is very important during BECE comprehension. You should spend about 15-20 minutes reading and understanding each passage. Read the questions first before reading the passage. This helps you know what to look for while reading. For example, if the passage is about market day in Lagos, look for information about prices, goods sold, and how people behave. Underline important points as you read. Answer questions in order, starting with the easiest ones to build confidence.
Class activity:
The class will be divided into groups. Each group will be given a comprehension passage and questions. They will have 20 minutes to read and answer the questions, then discuss their answers.
Evaluation questions:
1. How much time should you spend on a comprehension passage during BECE?
2. What should you do before reading the passage?
3. Why is it important to underline important points?
4. How can you improve your comprehension score?
Summary:
Good time management and careful reading are key to success in BECE comprehension questions.

topics.title: BECE grammar marathon
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify errors in sentences.
The students should be able to correct grammatical errors in sentences.
The students should be able to explain the difference between commonly confused words.
Introduction:
We have studied different parts of speech and grammatical rules in our previous lessons. Today we will practice identifying and correcting errors in sentences, which is important for the BECE examination.
Content:
Lexis and structure questions test your knowledge of vocabulary and grammar. Error spotting requires careful reading. Look for subject-verb agreement, tense consistency, and correct word usage. For example, in Nigeria, we say "I am going to the market" not "I am going to the market". Common errors include mixing up "their" and "there", or "your" and "you're". Practice with sentences like "The children plays football" which should be "The children play football". Also watch for double negatives like "I don't have no money" which should be "I don't have any money".
Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to create error-filled sentences. They will exchange with another pair who will identify and correct the errors.
Evaluation questions:
1. What is a common error in subject-verb agreement?
2. How would you correct the sentence "She don't like beans"?
3. What is the difference between "its" and "it's"?
4. Why is error spotting important in BECE?
Summary:
Practice with error spotting will help you improve your grammar skills for the BECE examination.

topics.title: BECE essay practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to plan an essay within 5 minutes.
The students should be able to write a coherent narrative essay.
The students should be able to write a convincing argumentative essay.
Introduction:
We have learned how to write different types of essays in our previous lessons. Today we will practice writing essays under time constraints, as required in the BECE examination.
Content:
For narrative essays, tell a story with a beginning, middle and end. Use past tense and descriptive language. For example, write about your experience during harmattan season. Describe the cold weather, the dusty harmattan haze, and how it affects daily life. For argumentative essays, state your position clearly and give reasons to support it. Use present tense and linking words like "however", "furthermore", and "in conclusion". For example, argue whether secondary school students should be allowed to use mobile phones in school. Plan your essay before writing: introduction, body paragraphs with examples, and conclusion. Time yourself to write within 40 minutes.
Class activity:
Students will be given essay topics and will have 5 minutes to plan, then 30 minutes to write either a narrative or argumentative essay.
Evaluation questions:
1. What are the three parts of a narrative essay?
2. What tense should you use in a narrative essay?
3. How do you structure an argumentative essay?
4. Why is planning important when writing under time pressure?
Summary:
Practice with timed essay writing will help you perform better in the BECE examination.

topics.title: BECE oral marathon
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to pronounce English sounds correctly.
The students should be able to identify stressed syllables in words.
The students should be able to complete dialogues appropriately.
Introduction:
We have practiced English sounds and intonation in our previous lessons. Today we will review all sounds and practice for the oral English part of the BECE examination.
Content:
English has 44 sounds, divided into vowels and consonants. Practice difficult sounds like /θ/ in "think" and /ð/ in "this". In Nigerian English, we sometimes replace these with /t/ and /d/. For oral English, pay attention to word stress. For example, in "NIGERia" the stress is on the first syllable, but in "naTIVE" it's on the second. Practice with common words used in exams. For dialogues, listen carefully to the question and give appropriate responses. For example, if asked "How was your weekend?" you could respond "It was fine, thank you. I visited my grandmother in the village." Record yourself to check your pronunciation and intonation.
Class activity:
Students will work in pairs practicing dialogues. One will ask questions, the other will respond, then they will switch roles. The teacher will provide feedback on pronunciation and stress.
Evaluation questions:
1. What are the two categories of English sounds?
2. How many syllables are stressed in the word "beautiful"?
3. What is the appropriate response to "How are you today?"
4. Why is word stress important in oral English?
Summary:
Regular practice with English sounds and dialogues will help you excel in the BECE oral examination.

topics.title: BECE literature marathon
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify main characters in set texts.
The students should be able to explain themes in set texts.
The students should be able to answer questions about characters and themes.
Introduction:
We have studied various literary texts in our previous lessons. Today we will revise the set texts for BECE, focusing on characters and themes that are commonly examined.
Content:
For narrative texts like "The Concubine" by Elechi Amadi, identify the main character such as Ihuoma. Understand her motivations and how she develops throughout the story. For themes, consider issues like fate, love, and tradition. For plays like "Lion and the Jewel" by Wole Soyinka, analyze characters like Sidi and Lakunle. Consider how their values clash. Themes might include modernity versus tradition. When answering questions, use specific examples from the text. For example, to show that Ihuoma is brave, mention how she faces difficult situations. Link characters and themes to show deeper understanding. Practice with past questions to familiarize yourself with the examination format.
Class activity:
Students will be divided into groups. Each group will be assigned a set text and will create character profiles and theme analyses to present to the class.
Evaluation questions:
1. Who is the main character in "The Concubine"?
2. What is a major theme in "Lion and the Jewel"?
3. How does Ihuoma's character develop throughout "The Concubine"?
4. Why is it important to use specific examples when answering literature questions?
Summary:
Understanding characters and themes in set texts is essential for success in the BECE literature examination.

topics.title: Mock examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete a full BECE English paper under timed conditions.
The students should be able to apply examination techniques.
The students should be able to identify areas of weakness for improvement.
Introduction:
We have practiced different sections of the BECE English examination in our previous lessons. Today we will take a full mock examination to prepare for the real BECE.
Content:
The mock examination will cover all sections of the BECE English paper: comprehension, lexis and structure, essay, oral literature, and literature questions. You will have the same time allocation as in the actual examination: 2 hours. Read all instructions carefully before starting. Manage your time wisely, spending about 30 minutes on comprehension, 30 minutes on lexis and structure, 40 minutes on essay, and 30 minutes on literature questions. For the oral section, listen carefully to the recording. Answer questions directly and concisely. After the examination, we will mark and review your papers together. This will help you understand your strengths and areas that need improvement before the actual BECE.
Class activity:
Students will write the full mock examination paper under timed conditions. After completion, papers will be marked and discussed in class.
Evaluation questions:
1. How much time should you allocate to each section of the BECE English paper?
2. What should you do before starting to answer questions?
3. Why is time management important during examinations?
4. How can reviewing your mock examination help you prepare for the real BECE?
Summary:
The mock examination provides valuable practice and feedback for the actual BECE English examination.

topics.title: Weakness clinics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify their weak areas in English.
The students should be able to explain strategies to improve in weak areas.
The students should be able to apply targeted practice to improve specific skills.
Introduction:
We have completed a mock examination in our previous lesson. Today we will identify and work on our weak areas in English to improve our performance in the BECE examination.
Content:
After reviewing your mock examination papers, identify areas where you lost marks. Common weak areas include comprehension inference questions, complex grammar structures, essay organization, and literature analysis. For comprehension, practice making inferences from passages. For grammar, focus on areas like reported speech and conditionals. For essays, practice planning and writing under time pressure. For literature, review character development and themes. Create a personal improvement plan with specific goals. For example, if you struggle with essay organization, practice writing outlines before essays. Use past questions and textbooks for targeted practice. Work with classmates who are strong in your weak areas to learn from them.
Class activity:
Students will form groups based on their identified weak areas. Each group will create practice exercises for their specific weakness and share with the class.
Evaluation questions:
1. How can you identify your weak areas in English?
2. What is a common weak area for students in BECE English?
3. Why is creating an improvement plan helpful?
4. How can working with classmates help improve your weak areas?
Summary:
Targeted practice on weak areas will help improve your overall performance in the BECE English examination.

topics.title: Speed and accuracy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete English exercises quickly without sacrificing accuracy.
The students should be able to apply techniques for improving reading speed.
The students should be able to minimize careless mistakes in examinations.
Introduction:
We have worked on improving specific skills in our previous lessons. Today we will focus on increasing our speed and accuracy in answering English questions, which is crucial for the BECE examination.
Content:
Speed and accuracy are both important for success in BECE. To improve reading speed, practice skimming and scanning techniques. Skim to get the general idea of a passage, scan to find specific information. For comprehension questions, read the questions first, then scan the passage for answers. For grammar exercises, recognize common patterns quickly. For example, identify that "if I ___, I ___" requires past perfect tense. To improve accuracy, check your work carefully. Look for common errors like subject-verb agreement, tense consistency, and proper punctuation. Practice with timed mini-tests to build speed while maintaining accuracy. For example, complete 10 comprehension questions in 15 minutes, then check your answers. Gradually reduce the time as you improve. Use techniques like underlining key words and eliminating obviously wrong options in multiple-choice questions.
Class activity:
Students will complete timed mini-tests for different sections of the BECE English paper. They will then check their answers and analyze any mistakes.
Evaluation questions:
1. What is the difference between skimming and scanning?
2. How can you improve accuracy in grammar exercises?
3. Why is it important to check your work carefully?
4. How can timed practice help improve both speed and accuracy?
Summary:
Developing both speed and accuracy through regular practice will help you perform better in the BECE examination.

topics.title: Final mock
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete a full BECE English paper under examination conditions.
The students should be able to apply all learned examination techniques.
The students should be able to evaluate their readiness for the actual BECE.
Introduction:
We have practiced various aspects of the BECE English examination in our previous lessons. Today we will take our final mock examination to assess our readiness for the actual BECE.
Content:
The final mock examination will be conducted under strict examination conditions to simulate the real BECE. You will have exactly 2 hours to complete all sections: comprehension, lexis and structure, essay, oral literature, and literature questions. No extra time will be given. Bring all required materials: pens, erasers, and ruler. Read all instructions carefully before starting. Manage your time wisely, moving from one section to another without getting stuck. For the essay section, choose the topic you know best and plan your answer before writing. For literature questions, use specific examples from the texts to support your points. After the examination, we will mark and review your papers together. This final review will help you make any last-minute adjustments before the actual BECE.
Class activity:
Students will write the final mock examination under strict examination conditions. Papers will be marked and discussed in detail to identify final areas for improvement.
Evaluation questions:
1. How should you prepare before starting the final mock examination?
2. What is the time allocation for each section of the BECE English paper?
3. How can you manage your time effectively during the examination?
4. What should you do if you encounter a difficult question?
Summary:
The final mock examination will help you assess your readiness and make final preparations for the actual BECE.

topics.title: BECE readiness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list important exam day tips.
The students should be able to explain how to stay calm during examinations.
The students should be able to identify necessary materials for the BECE examination.
Introduction:
We have completed all our preparations for the BECE English examination in our previous lessons. Today we will focus on final readiness tips and send-off blessings for the actual examination.
Content:
On exam day, arrive early at the examination center to avoid rushing. Bring all required materials: pens, pencils, erasers, ruler, and examination slip. Read all instructions carefully before starting each paper. Manage your time wisely, allocating appropriate time to each section. For difficult questions, skip and return to them later if time permits. Stay calm and positive throughout the examination. If you feel nervous, take deep breaths and focus on the questions. For the English paper, read passages carefully and answer questions directly. In the essay section, plan briefly before writing and check for errors. Remember that you have prepared well and trust your knowledge. After the examination, do not dwell on questions you found difficult. Focus on the next paper. We wish you all the best in your BECE examination. May you excel and achieve your goals.
Class activity:
Students will create a personal checklist of exam day preparations and share with the class. We will also have a brief send-off ceremony with words of encouragement.
Evaluation questions:
1. What materials should you bring to the BECE examination?
2. How can you manage your time during the examination?
3. What should you do if you encounter a difficult question?
4. Why is it important to stay calm during examinations?
Summary:
Proper preparation and a positive mindset will help you succeed in the BECE English examination.
